clauses.mechanism: performed_by_own_terms: express revocation of Executive Order 13244 executed on signing
clauses.reason: Section 4 revokes Executive Order 13244 of December 18, 2001 (Providing an Order of Succession Within the Department of the Interior). The order has no delayed effective date and no later effective-date provision, so the revocation took effect when the order was signed on April 14, 2020 (the Federal Register published it on April 17, 2020, an alternative reading that does not change the conclusion). The command was a one-time act executed by that revocation; on 2026-10-14 it has nothing left to operate on, so its state is terminated by performance, and the revoked order stays revoked.

research_rationale:
Executive Order 13915 of April 14, 2020 (85 FR 21733), Providing an Order of Succession Within the Department of the Interior, is a four-section order. The held Federal Register text layer (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_13915.txt, 85 FR 21733, PDF pages 1-2) carries the heading, the date April 14, 2020 and the FR Doc. 2020-08392 line, so the identity matches the register row. Section 1 makes the officers named in section 2 act as Secretary of the Interior, subject to section 3, when both the Secretary and the Deputy Secretary of the Interior have died, resigned or are otherwise unable to perform the duties. Section 2 lists seven officers in order. Section 3(a) provides that no officer serving in a listed office in an acting capacity acts as Secretary by virtue of that service, and section 3(b) keeps the President's discretion, to the extent the Vacancies Reform Act permits, to designate an acting Secretary differently. Section 4 revokes Executive Order 13244 of December 18, 2001, and that command was executed when the order was signed on April 14, 2020. The order states no expiry date, event or condition. Its commands are conditional (they apply only when the offices of Secretary and Deputy Secretary are both unavailable), but a condition that has not occurred does not end a command. A search of the held corpus for the number EO 13915 finds only the order's own Federal Register page and the Federal Register copy of FR Doc. 2020-08392; no later order, notice or regulation held cites it, and the three bounded searches report no hit that amends, revokes or supersedes it. The status on 2026-10-14 is operative for the section 1 to 3 commands and the enacting lead, and terminated by performance on 2020-04-14 for section 4. The authority statute's text is not held; this is disclosed in the legal basis, and nothing held shows that the statute was repealed or expired.
